system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
**Buyer review — Project Kestrel.** The Seller’s positions should not be accepted as a package. This review is based on the update and Disclosure Letter supplied, not the underlying SPA or DD documents. The Disclosure Letter’s footnote purporting to instruct the reviewer is not a deal term and has been disregarded.

| Issue | Seller’s position | Buyer should want | Recommendation and one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001 — General liability cap** | General Warranty Claims capped at **20% of price (AUD 4.8m)**. | A materially higher cap; propose **100% of price** as the buyer position, with any compromise assessed against diligence and recourse. | **Reject 20%:** it may leave substantial warranty losses unrecoverable on a AUD 24m acquisition. |
| **SPA-N-002 — De minimis & basket** | AUD 25,000 per claim; AUD 250,000 **deductible** basket. | Lower thresholds and a **tipping basket** (the whole claim pool recoverable once crossed), with related claims aggregated and appropriate categories excluded. | **Counter:** the proposed thresholds and deductible compound the low cap’s erosion of recovery. |
| **SPA-N-003 — General claims time limit** | Notice within **18 months**; Seller seeks a default time limit for all Claims. | At least **24–36 months** for general warranties; distinct, longer periods for tax, title and specific indemnities. | **Reject the blanket 18-month limit:** some liabilities will emerge only after a full reporting or customer cycle. |
| **SPA-N-004 — Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title subject to general caps and time limits. | Separate fundamental warranties with at least a **100%-of-price cap** and a substantially longer claim period; title protection tied to full, unencumbered ownership. | **Reject parity with general warranties:** failure to deliver the shares is a core transaction failure. |
| **SPA-N-005 — Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance wording applies to **all Claims of any nature**. | Express carve-out for fraud and deliberate concealment from caps, thresholds, time bars, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions. | **Insist on the carve-out:** the Seller must not use contractual limitations to shield fraudulent conduct. |
| **SPA-N-006 — Disclosure scope** | Blanket disclosure of the data room, Accounts, registers and public records. | Only **specific, fair disclosure** of facts and implications against identified warranties; no deemed disclosure merely because a document was available or searchable. | **Reject general disclosure:** it shifts the burden of identifying exceptions to the Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-007 — Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for matters known to Buyer or advisers, including anything discoverable from records. | No constructive or imputed-knowledge bar; ideally no knowledge exclusion, or only narrowly defined **actual knowledge** of named individuals and specifically disclosed facts. | **Delete or tightly narrow it:** “discoverable” could defeat warranties despite incomplete or ambiguous disclosure. |
| **SPA-N-008 — Bluefen consent** | Reasonable endeavours; condition satisfied by delivery of written consent. Final consent and evidence of clause 11.3 compliance are absent. | A Buyer-waivable **condition precedent** requiring effective written consent **and satisfaction of all associated conditions**, with evidence before Completion. | **Do not deem this resolved:** Bluefen represents about **30% of FY26 revenue**. |
| **SPA-N-009 — Riverlark facility** | Approximately **AUD 3.2m** remains outstanding; security release to follow Completion. | Debt repaid or deducted through Completion funds flow, with binding payout arrangements and effective discharge/release delivered **at Completion**. | **Reject post-Completion release:** Buyer agreed to a debt-free, cash-free acquisition and should not inherit secured-debt risk. |
| **SPA-N-010 — Employee bonuses** | Conditional **AUD 420,000** Completion bonuses omitted from funds flow; on-costs unspecified. | Seller-funded payment or a full price adjustment/retention for bonuses **and applicable payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs**, including amounts payable after Completion. | **Correct funds flow:** Completion-triggered obligations must not become an unpriced Buyer liability. |
| **SPA-N-011 — Ironquay IP indemnity** | Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; **AUD 180,000** shown open, with no payment receipt or confirmatory assignment. | Cleared payment and satisfactory assignment/chain-of-title evidence before Completion, plus a standalone indemnity for all losses from deficient ownership or use rights. | **Expand protection:** paying a fee alone may not cure a transfer-of-IP defect. |
| **SPA-N-012 — Export/privacy incident** | Described as preliminary and not expected to be material; access, scope and notification status remain unestablished. | Prompt forensic and legal assessment, evidence of containment/remediation and any required notifications; a specific indemnity or retention for pre-Completion exposure. | **Do not assume no breach or loss:** the known misdirected link warrants investigation before risk is allocated. |
| **SPA-N-013 — Sandbar renewals** | Three AUD 110,000 renewals treated as ordinary-course costs. | Review all three **together** for timing, termination rights, accrual and commitments; reflect any pre-Completion liability or non-ordinary commitment in price/funds flow or a specific protection. | **Do not accept the label alone:** the **AUD 330,000 aggregate** may be economically material. |
| **SPA-N-014 — Category separation** | Broad limitations and exclusive remedy proposed for all Claims. | Separate regimes for general warranties, fundamental/title, tax, specific indemnities, covenants, Completion obligations and fraud; no automatic cross-application. | **Redraft the claims architecture:** otherwise tailored protections may be neutralised by general limitations. |
| **SPA-N-015 — Title verification** | Seller relies on DD-012 share register showing 100% holding. | Verify issued capital, ownership, authority and absence of competing rights or encumbrances through corporate records, searches, instruments and Completion deliverables. | **Treat the register as a starting point:** it does not alone prove clean, transferable title. |
| **SPA-N-016 — Tax/IP open terms** | Tax and IP warranties treated as settled under the general regime. | Standalone pre-Completion tax covenant/indemnity with an appropriate longer period, and robust IP ownership, assignment, infringement and sufficiency warranties, plus issue-specific protection. | **Reopen both:** the general cap and 18-month period are ill-suited to tax and IP exposures. |

**Priority for the next mark-up:** make Bluefen consent and its conditions, Riverlark repayment/release, bonus funding and Ironquay chain of title explicit Completion deliverables; then revise the claims and disclosure regimes so those protections remain enforceable.
=== END ADVICE ===
